competencies.name: Frontend Engineering
competencies.description: Builds maintainable component-based interfaces with predictable state, data fetching, validation, and performance.
rubric_criteria: decomposes interfaces into cohesive components
manages local and server state explicitly
handles loading, empty, success, and error states
measures and improves user-visible performance

core_question.prompt: Design a frontend page that loads, filters, and edits a list of records from an API. Explain component boundaries, state, validation, loading and error behaviour, and how you would test it.

follow_ups.prompt: Which state belongs in the URL, server cache, and local component, and why?
How would you find and fix unnecessary renders or slow list rendering?

competencies.name: Web Accessibility and UX Quality
competencies.description: Creates keyboard-accessible, semantic, responsive interfaces with understandable feedback and inclusive interaction.
rubric_criteria: uses semantic controls before ARIA
supports keyboard and visible focus
associates labels, errors, and status messages
tests responsive and assistive-technology behaviour

core_question.prompt: A form looks correct with a mouse but is difficult to use with a keyboard and screen reader. Explain how you would audit it, prioritize fixes, and verify accessibility.

follow_ups.prompt: After a failed submission, where should focus move and how should errors be announced?
Which automated and manual checks would you combine?

competencies.name: Data Analysis and SQL
competencies.description: Transforms questions into reliable SQL analysis while checking data quality, grain, joins, and reproducibility.
rubric_criteria: defines metric and table grain before querying
uses joins and aggregation without duplication
checks missing, invalid, and outlier values
makes the analysis reproducible

core_question.prompt: You are asked why monthly active users dropped. Explain the data you need, SQL approach, quality checks, segmentation, and how you would communicate whether the drop is real.

follow_ups.prompt: How would you prevent a one-to-many join from inflating the user count?
Which checks distinguish a product change from a tracking failure?

competencies.name: Statistical Reasoning
competencies.description: Uses descriptive statistics, uncertainty, sampling, and experiment reasoning without overstating causal conclusions.
rubric_criteria: chooses a measure appropriate to the distribution
explains uncertainty and sampling limits
distinguishes correlation from causation
defines practical as well as statistical significance

core_question.prompt: An A/B test reports a small conversion increase. Explain how you would assess experiment validity, uncertainty, practical importance, and whether to recommend rollout.

follow_ups.prompt: What threats could make the observed difference non-causal?
When can a statistically significant result still be a poor product decision?

competencies.name: Data Visualization and Communication
competencies.description: Selects truthful visual encodings and communicates findings, uncertainty, and actions to the intended audience.
rubric_criteria: matches chart form to the analytical question
uses scales and labels without distortion
separates observation from interpretation
connects findings to an audience-relevant action

core_question.prompt: Design a dashboard for placement coordinators to understand student mock-interview participation and improvement. Explain metrics, charts, filters, caveats, and the decisions it supports.

follow_ups.prompt: Which chart would you use for change across repeated attempts and why?
How would you prevent the dashboard from exaggerating small changes?

competencies.name: Machine Learning Fundamentals
competencies.description: Frames prediction problems, prepares data, selects suitable baselines, and recognizes leakage, imbalance, and overfitting.
rubric_criteria: defines inputs, target, unit of prediction, and constraints
creates a meaningful baseline
prevents train-test leakage
connects model choice to data and operational needs

core_question.prompt: You need to predict whether a support ticket will miss its response-time target. Explain problem framing, dataset construction, leakage prevention, baseline, features, and validation.

follow_ups.prompt: Give one feature that would leak future information and explain why.
What simple baseline must the model outperform?

competencies.name: Model Evaluation and Responsible ML
competencies.description: Chooses decision-relevant metrics, evaluates slices and uncertainty, and documents limitations and responsible-use boundaries.
rubric_criteria: chooses metrics based on error costs
evaluates relevant data slices
reports uncertainty and limitations
defines monitoring and non-use boundaries

core_question.prompt: A classifier has high accuracy but misses many important positive cases. Explain how you would evaluate it, select a threshold, inspect subgroup performance, and report limitations.

follow_ups.prompt: When would recall matter more than precision in this problem?
How would you investigate a large performance gap between legitimate evaluation slices?

competencies.name: ML Engineering
competencies.description: Builds reproducible training and inference pipelines with versioned data, models, validation, and monitoring.
rubric_criteria: versions code, configuration, data references, and checkpoints
keeps preprocessing consistent between training and inference
validates inputs and fails safely
monitors data quality, latency, and model behaviour

core_question.prompt: Turn a trained model notebook into a reliable prediction service. Explain artifact versioning, preprocessing parity, API validation, deployment, monitoring, and rollback.

follow_ups.prompt: How would you guarantee that training and inference use the same transformations?
What artifacts and metadata are required to restore the previous model safely?

competencies.name: Cloud and Platform Fundamentals
competencies.description: Designs a small secure cloud deployment with suitable compute, networking, storage, identity, and cost awareness.
rubric_criteria: selects services from stated requirements
uses least-privilege identity and secret handling
explains network and data flow
considers availability, observability, and cost

core_question.prompt: Deploy a small web API and database for university users in the cloud. Explain compute, networking, secrets, storage, backups, monitoring, and cost controls.

follow_ups.prompt: How would the application receive database credentials without committing a secret?
Which failure would you design for first and how?

competencies.name: CI/CD and Automation
competencies.description: Automates repeatable build, test, security-check, release, and rollback workflows with controlled promotion.
rubric_criteria: defines fast and reliable quality gates
keeps build artifacts immutable across environments
separates approval from execution
provides safe deployment and rollback

core_question.prompt: Design a CI/CD pipeline for a containerized API. Explain triggers, tests, security checks, artifact handling, environment promotion, deployment verification, and rollback.

follow_ups.prompt: Why should production use the exact artifact tested in staging?
Which signal should automatically stop or reverse a deployment?

competencies.name: Containers, Observability, and Reliability
competencies.description: Packages services consistently and uses logs, metrics, traces, health checks, and incident practice to operate them reliably.
rubric_criteria: builds minimal reproducible container images
distinguishes readiness from liveness
uses logs, metrics, and traces for different questions
defines actionable alerts and incident verification

core_question.prompt: A containerized service becomes slow and sometimes restarts. Explain how you would use health checks, logs, metrics, traces, resource limits, and a safe fix verification.

follow_ups.prompt: What is the difference between liveness and readiness, and how can a wrong check cause an outage?
Which alert would be actionable before users report the problem?
